newsitem.title: NORWAY: STATOIL TO SUBMIT PLAN FOR N.SEA HULDRA FIELD.
newsitem.headline: STATOIL TO SUBMIT PLAN FOR N.SEA HULDRA FIELD.

text.p: Norway's Statoil said on Thursday it will submit a plan for the development and operation (PDO) of the Huldra field in the North Sea to the Norwegian authorities in October.

Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the decision to submit a PDO was taken by the licensees after Norway's Gas Supply Committee last spring allowed the field to supply gas to European buyers from 1999 or 2000.
Licensees in Huldra are operator Statoil (Den norske stats oljeselskap AS), Conoco and Total.
The likely development solution for Huldra, which lies in blocks 30/2 and 30/3 in the Oseberg-Troll area, is a wellhead platform equipped for first-stage separation, Statoil said.
Gas, condensate and water will be separated and piped to a nearby platform. Before the PDO is submitted, the partners must clarify which field Huldra will be tied-back to, it said.
Recoverable reserves at the field are put at 20 billion cubic metres of gas and just under 50 million barrels of oil and condensate.
